title: Emrys and the Wreck
premise: Odile Blackwood flies supply runs into the rainforest interior, keeping her head down to pay off a debt she inherited from her late father. When a government survey team vanishes near a drowned valley, she is pressured—by debt collectors and officials alike—to fly the search, and crash-lands in the flood zone with Emrys Vale, a quiet stranger who knows too much about the missing team. As monsoon rains trap them together on a leaking boat, Odile discovers Emrys is the survey's disgraced cartographer, hiding evidence that the government caused the disaster and wants buried. Hunted by the survey's security chief and betrayed by the man who holds her debt, Odile must choose between flying home safe and exposing the truth. In the end she burns her father's debt papers, testifies with Emrys at her side, and finds that belonging was never something she had to buy.
about_author: Sebastian Delacroix is the pen name of a former bush mechanic who spent six years patching floatplanes along remote river routes before turning to fiction. He writes adventure stories about people who live where maps run out.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She flies medicine and gossip into river settlements, counting every gallon of fuel against her father's debt. A routine landing nearly kills her when the strip floods. Beat: competence masking exhaustion; establish her isolation as armor.

chapters.title: Compass and Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the trading post, debt collector Harrow Voss reminds her the note comes due after the wet season. She checks her dead father's compass out of habit. Beat: the debt made concrete; her fear of being owned.

chapters.title: The Survey That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Officials charter her to resupply a government survey team in the drowned valley of Kestrel Reach. The team misses two scheduled contacts. Beat: unease; the first crack in her invisibility.

chapters.title: Gear Without Tracks
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Flying low over the reach, she spots abandoned camp gear, no bodies, no tracks, no smoke. Radio calls go unanswered. Beat: dread; the landscape itself feels wrong.

chapters.title: Ordered Down
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Command insists she land and investigate despite rising weather. She argues, complies, hates herself for it. Beat: duty pressing against instinct; foreshadowing the theme of forced choices.

chapters.title: The Man in the Reeds
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Hidden in the flooded reeds, Emrys watches the plane descend, deciding whether to reveal himself or stay ghost. He steps out. Beat: his guilt and calculation; two solitudes meeting.

chapters.title: Stranger's Hands
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Emrys helps Odile secure the plane as the first storm bands hit. He claims to be a survivor but answers questions too carefully. Beat: wary alliance; attraction flickering under suspicion.

chapters.title: Monsoon Wall
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The storm closes the valley; takeoff is impossible. They shelter in the wrecked survey camp and find the team's logs half-burned. Beat: trapped; the mystery deepens alongside intimacy.

chapters.title: What the Logs Said
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Flashback: Emrys was the survey's cartographer. His maps flagged unstable dam foundations; his superiors redlined them and proceeded anyway. Beat: confession withheld; guilt established.

chapters.title: Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. With the plane's radio drowned, they salvage the survey's aluminum boat—it leaks. Emrys patches it while Odile watches the water rise over the runway. Beat: forced cooperation; small trust earned through work.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: Both POV. They boat toward the lower station through drowned forest, navigating by Odile's compass and Emrys's memory. Beat: fragile partnership; banter as deflection from fear.

chapters.title: The Drowned Village
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. They pass a village evacuated years ago for the dam project; Emrys goes silent. Odile realizes he carries more than survival. Beat: empathy growing; the cost of 'progress' made visible.

chapters.title: Night Signals
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A searchlight sweeps the water—the survey's private security, led by Chief Ansel Roque, hunting witnesses. They kill their lamp and drift. Beat: hunted; stakes shift from weather to men.

chapters.title: Roque
chapters.summary: Roque's POV. Roque reports to the ministry liaison that the cartographer survived and must not reach the coast. He orders the river watched. Beat: antagonist revealed; cold institutional menace.

chapters.title: Bail and Bailing
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. All night they bail water and share stories by necessity. Emrys admits he was on the team; not yet why it vanished. Beat: intimacy under pressure; love beginning as reliance.

chapters.title: The Second Wreck
chapters.summary: Both POV. They find the survey's own boat wrecked against a strainer log—one survivor's jacket, blood, nothing else. Beat: horror; the vanished team's fate partially answered.

chapters.title: Confession in the Rain
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys tells all: the dam failed early, the team found the sabotage cover-up, Roque cut them loose in the flood. He ran with the evidence. Beat: full disclosure; Odile's choice crystallizes.

chapters.title: What Staying Invisible Costs
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile rages—she wanted no part of this—but realizes Voss's debt and Roque's hunt mean neutrality is gone. Beat: the theme stated; she stops pretending she can opt out.

chapters.title: Voss on the Wire
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At a ranger relay, a garbled message: Voss has taken a lien on her plane. Her escape route home now belongs to someone else. Beat: betrayal; the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Lower Station
chapters.summary: Both POV. They reach the lower station to find it stripped and Roque waiting in ambush. A firefight across the boathouse; they flee downriver as the station burns. Beat: action peak of act two; no way back.

chapters.title: Rapids
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The leaking boat takes the gorge rapids; Emrys is thrown, Odile hauls him aboard half-drowned. Beat: near-death; unspoken love surfaces in panic.

chapters.title: Island of Driftwood
chapters.summary: Both POV. Stranded on a shingle bar, they dry out, repair the hull, and admit what they are to each other—not quite lovers, no longer strangers. Beat: tenderness; belonging chosen, not bought.

chapters.title: Roque's Offer
chapters.summary: Roque's POV. Roque corners them by radio: hand over the evidence and he'll clear Odile's debts and let them go. Beat: temptation; the exact price of her freedom named.

chapters.title: The Counterfeit Compass
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile proposes a bluff: give Roque a decoy drive hidden in her father's compass case while Emrys carries the real evidence. Beat: agency reclaimed; her father's legacy repurposed.

chapters.title: Handoff at the Weir
chapters.summary: Both POV. The exchange goes wrong—Roque searches Emrys first. Odile's bluff buys seconds, not safety; they scatter into the mangroves. Beat: plan fraying; separation anxiety.

chapters.title: Alone in the Green
chapters.summary: Split POV. Each believes the other captured. Odile reaches an old fire tower; Emrys evades dogs in the swamp. Beat: despair and resolve; love tested by absence.

chapters.title: The Tower Signal
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. From the tower, Odile rigs the broken radio and broadcasts the survey cover-up on open channels—every pilot, every settlement hears it. Beat: turning point; truth as weapon.

chapters.title: Pilots Rising
chapters.summary: New character POV (Marta, rival pilot). River pilots who owe Odile favors begin flying interference, jamming Roque's boats with false sightings. Beat: community; she was never as alone as she believed.

chapters.title: Reunion at the Salt Line
chapters.summary: Both POV. Emrys reaches the coast where Marta's seaplane waits; Odile arrives minutes behind, pursued. They reunite under gunfire and lift off. Beat: catharsis; the arc's emotional payoff.

chapters.title: Storm Chase
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Roque's floatplane pursues them into a squall line. Odile flies terrain she knows like breath and loses him in a canyon. Beat: mastery vindicated; her skills as identity.

chapters.title: The Capital's Door
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. They deliver the evidence to a federal auditor—and discover Voss sits on the ministry board that signed off the dam. Beat: the rot goes higher; hope complicated.

chapters.title: Debt Called Due
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Voss offers to bury the audit if Odile recants, erasing her debt. He invokes her father's signature. Beat: final temptation; everything she's wanted offered for silence.

chapters.title: Burning the Note
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile refuses and burns the debt papers in front of him, choosing exposure over relief. Beat: climax of character; the price of survival paid willingly.

chapters.title: Hearing in the Wet Season
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The inquiry opens; Emrys testifies to the redlined maps. Roque's chain of command unravels; Voss stalls. Beat: justice grinding; tension held through procedure.

chapters.title: Roque's Last Flight
chapters.summary: Roque's POV. Ordered to destroy remaining records, Roque instead flees with them—and Odile is asked to help intercept. Beat: antagonist's endgame; her past weaponized one last time.

chapters.title: Kestrel Reach Again
chapters.summary: Both POV. Odile flies the interception over the drowned valley where it began; Roque ditches in the floodwater and is taken alive by the pilots' cordon. Beat: full-circle climax; the valley gives up its secret.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The audit lands: officials indicted, the dam condemned, settlements funded for the drowned villages. Emrys is cleared; Odile's name is clean. Beat: resolution of plot; grief for what can't be restored.

chapters.title: The Plane Is Hers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. With the lien voided, Odile owns her plane outright for the first time. She repaints the tail with her father's compass rose. Beat: inheritance transformed from burden to gift.

chapters.title: Runways South
chapters.summary: Both POV. Emrys asks what comes next; Odile offers him the right-hand seat—not because she needs him, but because she chooses him. First kiss on the dock at dawn. Beat: love without debt; belonging freely given.

chapters.title: First Light, Full Tank
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Epilogue: a new season's first run, medicine and mail and no secrets. Over Kestrel Reach, the water is being lowered. Beat: peace earned; flight as freedom, finally unburdened.
